newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee full covertibility to be delayed - RBI.
newsitem.headline: India rupee full covertibility to be delayed - RBI.

text.p: Plans to make the Indian rupee fully convertible on the capital account will be delayed, a top official of the central bank was quoted as saying on Friday.

The Business Standard newspaper quoted the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) chief general manager P.K. Biswas as saying that "the capital account convertibility may continue to elude the country for longer than expected."
"He (Biswas) personally felt that the convertibility would become a reality only by the end of the century," it said in a report from the southern city of Bangalore.
Biswas was addressing a seminar organised by the Greater Mysore Chamber of Commerce and Industry on Thursday.
He said full convertibility would be based on three factors - sufficient foreign exchange reserve, inflation and the fiscal deficit.
"It would not be possible to open indiscriminately the external commercial borrowings as it would spiral the inflation curve," the paper quoted Biswas as saying.
He said India received a foreign exchange inflow of about $10.0 billion a year. Out of this, about $4.0 billion was from external commercial borrowings.

"There is a need to create a market to absorb the entire inflow while having inflation under control and the fiscal deficit at 4.5 percent of the gross domestic product, the RBI official was quoted as saying.
The RBI has appointed a panel to study full rupee convertibility on the capital account. The panel, according to a recent government announcement, must submit its report in three months.

Unveiling the budget for financial year 1997/98 (April-March) on February 28, Finance Minister P. Chidambaram told parliament that India had met some of the conditions necessary for full convertibility on the capital account.
